examples.solution_text:
All four corners have right-angle marks. Opposite sides have matching ticks.
Rectangle.
All four sides equal is not given, so a square is not guaranteed. Turning the diagram does not change the marks.

examples.question_text:
Is every square a rectangle? Is every rectangle a square?
Give a reason for each answer.
examples.solution_text:
Yes. A square has four right angles and equal opposite sides, so it meets the rectangle definition.
No. A rectangle can have two longer sides and two shorter sides. A square needs all four sides equal.

Following the boundary clockwise from $P$ gives $P$, $S$, $Q$, then $R$.
$PSQR$.

examples.question_text:
Give the most specific name guaranteed by each description.
a. A quadrilateral has four equal sides and four right angles.
b. A quadrilateral has consecutive side lengths $4\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$, $4\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$. No right angles are given.
c. A quadrilateral has consecutive side lengths $5\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$.
d. A quadrilateral has four equal sides. No right angles are given.
e. In quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB\parallel CD$, $AB=7\text{ cm}$ and $CD=11\text{ cm}$. The corner at $D$ is a right angle.
examples.solution_text:
a. Square: four equal sides and four right angles.
b. Parallelogram: both pairs of opposite sides are equal. Four right angles are not given, so a rectangle is not guaranteed.
c. Kite: the two $5\text{ cm}$ sides meet at one corner, and the two $8\text{ cm}$ sides meet at another. These are equal adjacent pairs.
d. Rhombus: all four sides are equal. Four right angles are not given, so a square is not guaranteed.
e. Trapezium: one pair of opposite sides is parallel. Their unequal lengths rule out a parallelogram and therefore a rectangle; one right angle does not change this.

examples.question_text:
A quadrilateral has four right angles and consecutive side lengths $4\text{ cm}$, $9\text{ cm}$, $4\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$.
List every classification it has from quadrilateral, trapezium, parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square and kite.
Use the definitions that a trapezium has at least one pair of parallel opposite sides and a kite has two pairs of equal adjacent sides.
examples.solution_text:
Rectangle: it has four right angles and equal opposite sides.
It is also a parallelogram, because both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, and a trapezium, because it has at least one parallel pair. It has four sides, so it is a quadrilateral.
The classifications are quadrilateral, trapezium, parallelogram and rectangle.
Adjacent sides have different lengths, so it is neither a kite nor a rhombus nor a square.

coverage.summary: Kept all three existing examples exactly and added two source-based examples covering stated-property classification and all applicable classifications, with changed numerical values. Every distinct assessed method is covered. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither changed nor re-audited. No files were written; final-size rendering and label verification remain for the capture stage.

examples.derivation: a. Four equal sides and four right angles guarantee a square. b. Consecutive lengths 4, 7, 4, 7 give equal opposite pairs, guaranteeing a parallelogram; right angles are not guaranteed. c. Consecutive lengths 5, 8, 8, 5 give two equal adjacent pairs, guaranteeing a kite. d. Four equal sides guarantee a rhombus; right angles are not guaranteed. e. AB and CD are parallel but have unequal lengths, so the shape is a trapezium and cannot be a parallelogram or rectangle. These conclusions follow the supplied definitions and source classification exercises.

Four right angles guarantee a rectangle and therefore two parallel opposite pairs. Its classifications are quadrilateral, trapezium, parallelogram and rectangle under the supplied inclusive definition. Consecutive lengths 4, 9, 4, 9 make every adjacent pair unequal, excluding kite, rhombus and square.
